title: Complaints about the turnout for the New Christy Minstrels
body: A letter from Dan Gritton in the last Herald of the year criticised attendance at the New Christy Minstrels show, the earliest recorded grumble about an empty house at a campus concert.
note: The letter is real: "Gritton, Dan. Criticizes Attendance at New Christy Minstrels Show" (and a second, "Hayden, Phyllis. Timing Hurt New Christy Minstrels Show"). But nothing in the source ties the concert to Associated Students, and "earliest recorded grumble" is an unsourced superlative. Filed as a concert entry on an unattributed campus show.

title: Wilson Pickett headlines a soul concert
body: The Herald's front page for 14 December 1967 announced a soul concert that night starring Wilson Pickett. It is the biggest single act the record shows on campus in Menser's year.
note: "Soul Concert Tonight Stars Wilson Pickett" is in 47:15 for 14 December, so the date holds. But the source gives no sponsor, so nothing connects the concert to Associated Students, and front-page placement plus "biggest single act" are not shown by an article index.

title: Pacific Gas and Electric flops at Homecoming
body: Ernie Hearion's review in the Herald was headed "Utilities Down Sharply on Entertainment Market." The 1971 Talisman was blunter, writing that Pacific Gas and Electric turned on very few when they appeared as part of Homecoming weekend.
note: Both quotations are genuine: Hearion's "Utilities Down Sharply on Entertainment Market" (50:13) and the Talisman's "Utilities stocks went down as Pacific Gas and Electric 'turned on' very few when they appeared as part of Homecoming weekend." But the yearbook places the concert in Homecoming weekend, which the same 50:13 issue recaps as already past; 13 October 1970 was a Tuesday and is the review's publication date, not the concert date.

title: Reginald Glass on block-booking and the price of entertainment
body: Reginald Glass, the first black vice president of the Associated Students, headed the activities committee and co-ordinated student cultural activities, signing the contracts for concerts and speakers. In the 1972 Talisman he said he had wanted to do something about the high prices of entertainment but found it hard to reduce them because block-booking with schools in Kentucky and Tennessee was difficult to arrange, and that he had hoped to bring in different types of groups so most student factions would be satisfied at some point in the year.
note: Only a caption is confirmed: "Reginald Glass, vice-president of Associated Students, is signing contracts." The quoted views — wanting to do something about high prices, block-booking with Kentucky and Tennessee schools being hard to arrange, hoping to satisfy most student factions — are not in the 1972 Talisman text; "block booking" and "high prices" return no match. Herald 51:53 does carry "Moore, Chris. Black Vice-President Finds Race is No Problem – Reginald Glass," but that issue is not the cited source.

title: Edmund Muskie calls for Nixon's impeachment
body: ASG's lecture series brought Senator Edmund Muskie of Maine on 11 December 1973 to speak on 'The Restoration of Confidence'. Muskie called for the impeachment of President Nixon, saying he had decided after much soul-searching on the night of the Saturday Night Massacre that it was the only way to raise the issue.
note: The cited Herald 53:26, 4 Dec 1973 carries only "Sen. Edmund Muskie Lecture Set for Dec. 11" - an advance notice a week before the event. It cannot support the topic quotation, the impeachment call, or the Saturday Night Massacre remark. All of that, plus the ASG tie, is in the 1974 Talisman (topic "The Restoration of Confidence"; caption "In an ASG-sponsored lecture, Senator Edmund Muskie called for the impeachment of President Nixon"), which is not cited.

title: Pure Prairie League plays two shows, the first ruined by the sound
body: ASG billed Pure Prairie League for two shows in Van Meter on 31 January 1975. Sound problems ruined most of the first set at 7:30 and bassist Mike Reilly asked the 9:30 audience whether anyone had seen the first show; the problems were fixed and the second show was first-rate.
note: The cited Herald Vol. 50 No. 31, 24 Jan 1975 carries only "Associated Student Government Bills Pure Prairie League" - an advance notice a week before the show. The whole review is in the uncited 1975 Talisman: "bassist Mike Rieley... asked the audience of the 9:30 concert on Jan. 31... The 7:30 show was not as bad as Rieley said - it was worse. Sound problems ruined most of the first act... All sound problems were solved, however, before the second show, which was first-rate." (A Talisman caption elsewhere misdates the same concert to October 30.)

title: Andrae Crouch and the Disciples in the Garrett ballroom
body: The soul gospel group Andrae Crouch and the Disciples performed in the Garrett Conference Center ballroom on 8 February 1976. The Talisman lists it among the year's ASG entertainment alongside the free concerts.
note: The 1976 Talisman does say "Gospel group Andrae Crouch and the Disciples, a soul gospel group, performed in the Garrett Conference Center ballroom on Feb. 8" - but it does not tie the show to ASG in any way. The entry's assertion that "The Talisman lists it among the year's ASG entertainment alongside the free concerts" overstates what the source does: it is an on-campus event with no student-government attribution.

title: Homecoming concert booked without a signed contract
body: A week before the Homecoming show the Herald reported that Western had never signed a contract with Sunshine Promotions, the firm that had booked Player and Exile for 3 November. Sunshine refused to sign because the university demanded a $100,000 performance bond guaranteeing that all bills would be paid; the company said Indiana insurers wanted 100 percent collateral and a $2,000 service fee for it. The Homecoming concert went ahead on an oral agreement alone.

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 54, No. 19, 26 October 1978

note: Herald 10-26-1978, Vol. 54 No. 19 confirmed. The front-page story 'Concert contract hasn't been signed' supports the core: Western has not signed with Sunshine because the firm won't post a $100,000 bond required by the university; the bond would guarantee all bills related to the three concerts would be paid; Player and Exile booked for a Nov. 3 concert; Sybesma cites '100 percent collateral and $2,000 service fee insurance companies say they must have.' TWO PROBLEMS. (1) The closing sentence, 'The Homecoming concert went ahead on an oral agreement alone,' cannot come from this issue - the concert was still eight days in the future. I read the full continuation on p.3; there is no mention of an oral or verbal agreement anywhere in the issue. That wording appears in the 9 November editorial (record 3429), which says the show was 'booked and produced on an emergency basis with only an [oral] agreement between Sunshine and the university.' Cite that issue instead. (2) 'Indiana insurers' is not in this source, which says only 'insurance companies'; the Indiana detail comes from Talisman 1979. Also 'Sunshine refused to sign' overstates it - the article says the firm won't post the bond, and Sybesma said his company might agree to put up money before each concert.

title: Randy Crawford and the Crusaders play free to 1,409
body: The jazz group The Crusaders, with Randy Crawford opening, played Diddle Arena free to full-time students on 26 April. Turnstiles registered 1,409 people at the intermission, of whom only about 1,200 were students, less than 10 percent of the student body, and an estimated 200 tickets sold to non-students brought in about $1,000. The university paid $11,396 in expenses, including $6,000 for The Crusaders and $1,000 for Crawford, and assistant university centers director Tim Nemeth said afterwards, "More than likely, that's the last free show you'll see."
money: $11,396 in expenses; $6,000 to The Crusaders, $1,000 to Randy Crawford; about $1,000 taken at the gate

src.label: College Heights Herald, Vol. 54, No. 59, 1 May 1979

note: Every figure is exact, but the source explicitly attributes the show to the university rather than to student government. Herald 5-1-1979, Vol. 54 No. 59, '1,409 attend Crusaders' concert': Thursday concert in Diddle Arena, free for full-time students; '1,409 people had been registered by the turnstiles... at the intermission'; 'Only 1,200 students - less than 10 percent of the student population - attended'; 'An estimated 200 tickets were sold to non-students, bringing in about $1,000'; 'the university paid about $11,396 in expenses for the concert, including $6,000 for The Crusaders and $1,000 for Ms. Crawford'; and the Nemeth quote 'More than likely, that's the last free show you'll see.' ASG appears nowhere in the article, and Nemeth is quoted saying 'the university, not Sunshine Promotions, handled all the expenses involved.' Talisman 1979 p.79 likewise files it under concerts Western sponsored 'independent of Sunshine Promotions.' Keep it only if the archive covers university-run shows, and reword to drop any implied ASG credit.

title: ASG hosts the second statewide student government conference
body: ASG played host to the second annual statewide student government conference from Friday 27 March to Sunday 29 March at the American Plaza on Scottsville Road, with registration at $18 and open to all students. President Tim Todd expected about 50 student leaders, down from about 65 at the first conference, which ASG had also hosted, and said hosting would cost between $400 and $500. Saturday seminars covered leadership, communication and financial aid, with the Council on Higher Education flying in a financial aid consultant from Washington and sending its director, Gary S. Cox.
note: REJECT - announcement written up as a completed event. Herald 62:48, 26 Mar 1987 is headlined "Student government conference TO BE HELD Friday through Sunday" and reads "Western's Associated Student Government WILL BE HOST to the second annual statewide student government conference tomorrow through Sunday." Nothing in this issue reports that the conference took place; a follow-up issue would be needed. Everything else in the entry does match the source, including the figure I initially misread from OCR: the page image plainly reads "About 65 went to last year's conference, also hosted by ASG" - so the entry's "about 65" is correct. Also confirmed: about 50 expected, American Plaza on Scottsville Road, President Tim Todd, "Registration is $18", "Hosting the conference will cost between $400 and $500", CHE flying in a financial aid consultant from Washington D.C., and director D. Gary S. Cox attending. Fix the tense and the dating and this becomes usable.

title: Project Western Week and the Don't Trash The Spirit clean-up
body: SGA ran Project Western Week from Monday 8 February, its biggest event a mass campus clean-up on Wednesday 10 February under the motto Don't Trash The Spirit. Students gathered with bin bags at about 3:30 p.m. at the New Co-Ed and New Sorority dorms, spread out across the width of campus and finished at Cherry Hall, and about 600 people were expected. The campus was divided into 23 sections taken by organisations that had signed up by 5 February and that stayed responsible for their areas until the end of term, with the group keeping the cleanest area to receive $500 from SGA.
money: $500 prize to the organisation with the cleanest area
note: REJECT for the 10 February clean-up specifically - it is announced, not reported. Herald 68:35, 9 Feb 1993, p.6, "SGA news: Students arm themselves with trash bags to clean up campus" opens "DON'T BE SURPRISED TOMORROW to see a mass of students, armed with trash bags, marching up the Hill." This page had no OCR layer, so I read it as an image. Everything else matches exactly: motto "Don't Trash The Spirit"; "The event will be the biggest part of Project Western Week, said Student Government Association President Joe Rains. Project Western Week began Monday and lasts through the week"; "Students will begin picking up trash around 3:30 p.m. at the New Co-Ed and New Sorority dorms. The group will spread out the width of the campus, and conclude their march at Cherry Hall"; "About 600 people are expected to attend"; "The campus will be divided into 23 sections"; "organizations had until Feb. 5 to sign up"; responsible "until the end of the semester"; "the group with the cleanest area gets $500 from SGA." The $500 is genuinely in the source. Only the past tense on the 10 Feb clean-up needs fixing; the 8 Feb start of the week is properly supported.

title: Dialogue Day puts administrators in Niteclass
body: President Donald Smith announced that 6 April 1994 would be Dialogue Day, when students could talk with administrators in Niteclass between noon and 2 p.m. The public relations committee handed out flyers for it alongside flyers for the coming election. It was one of a run of access events SGA staged that spring, with the memorial tree programme, the security phones due by 26 April and the campus clean-up.
note: REJECT as dated - announcement only. SGA minutes, 29 Mar 1994: "President Smith reported that April 6 is 'Dialogue Day'. Students can talk with administrators in Niteclass from 12 p.m. - 2 p.m." and, under PUBLIC RELATIONS, "Lena Sweeten-Garner passed out flyers concerning the upcoming election and Dialogue Day." So the announcement and the flyers are solid, but nothing shows the 6 April event happened or that anyone attended; an entry dated 1994-04-06 asserting it took place goes beyond the record. The supporting details are otherwise accurate - the same minutes give "Security phones should be in place by April 26" and the Memorial Tree programme.

title: Provide-A-Ride starts giving students rides home
body: SGA's Provide-A-Ride service began carrying students in January 1997. Within a week the Herald was warning that the programme needed more student support to survive.

src.label: Herald 72:29, 23 Jan 1997 - Batcheldor, "Student Government Association Gives Rides to Students"

note: The record confirms only 'Batcheldor, Matt. Student Government Association Gives Rides to Students', 23 Jan 1997. It does not name the service 'Provide-A-Ride', does not say the service began in January 1997, and contains nothing about the Herald warning a week later that the programme needed more student support to survive. Issue is Vol. 72, No. 31, not 72:29.

title: The autumn banquet closes the semester
body: SGA held its autumn banquet straight after the Congress meeting on 2 December 2003, the last meeting of the term, and had its yearbook photograph taken there. The calendar for the year also records a Parents' Weekend lunch on 20 September, a campus lighting and safety walk on 13 October, and forums on campus safety, plus-minus grading, academic issues, housing and elections.
note: The cited Events Calendar does not support the headline claim. Its December 2003 panel shows only '2 Congress Meeting 5:00 DUC 305' - no banquet, no yearbook photograph, and no indication this was the last meeting of the term. The calendar does support the second sentence: Parents' Weekend Lunch on 20 September, Campus Lighting/Safety Walk on 13 October, and forums on campus safety (11 Sep), plus/minus grading (9 Oct), academic issues (13 Nov), housing (12 Feb) and elections (11 Mar). A different, uncited SGA page (newsFall2003) does announce that 'The SGA banquet will be held right after the Congress meeting on Tuesday', but that is prospective and still says nothing about a yearbook photograph.

title: Transcript voucher programme launched
body: On 28 February 2012 the senate allocated $1,225 for a transcript voucher programme, offering 175 free official transcripts, two per student, at a time when a transcript cost $7. Cory Dodds, SGA director of information technology and a bill author, said he hoped it would become an SGA staple like the free scantrons and blue books. Registrar Freida Eggleton worked with SGA on the rollout. The same meeting passed $500 for five $100 Study Away scholarships and $2,300 in Scholar Development and Study Abroad awards.
money: $1,225 for 175 vouchers; $500 in Study Away scholarships; $2,300 in grants

src.label: Herald, 29 Feb 2012 - "SGA to launch transcript voucher program"

note: The 29 Feb 2012 article supports the core allocation - 'The first bill passed at the SGA meeting Tuesday night allocated $1,225 for transcript vouchers... A total of 175 vouchers will be available with a limit of two per student' - plus '$500 from general senate funding... five $100 scholarships' and 'Additional $2,300 in funding for Scholar Development Grant Awards and Study Abroad Awards'. But three claims are absent from it: the $7 transcript price is never given (it is a division of 1,225 by 175, and appears only in a different, later article); Cory Dodds is not quoted or mentioned at all, so the 'SGA staple like the free scantrons and blue books' line is unsupported; and Registrar Freida Eggleton does not appear. Per the standard on amounts the source does not give, this fails.
